title: Read Human Nature Through Incentives
coreMove: Read the stated reason and the payoff structure together before trusting either alone.
sourcePressure: The source says people often act from self-interest but also from reputation, reciprocity, fairness, approval, fear of humiliation, obedience, imitation, similarity, praise, familiarity, and status pressure. One-shot encounters make selfish behavior easier.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is cynical motive-reading where every explanation is a lie. The real move is to see mixed motives and the payoff structure that makes some behavior predictable.

hook: People do what they are paid to do
counterintuition: The stated reason is always false
examples: friend asks for a favor with no texture

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: independent restaurant changing a tip-pooling rule before summer patio season
exampleSpecs.audience: Claire, a general manager hearing servers defend fairness in opposite directions
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a rushed policy turns good servers against hosts during the busiest month
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire writes each role's visible payoff beside its fairness claim before deciding which complaint is principle and which is pressure from the new split
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "So fairness means the bar keeps the patio tips?" on a receipt-strewn service station

exampleSpecs.domain: open-source maintainer deciding whether to accept a sponsor's roadmap request
exampleSpecs.audience: Lukas, a volunteer maintainer praised by a company that now wants priority work
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether praise and funding quietly move the project away from user need
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lukas pins the sponsor email next to the issue backlog and labels which request serves the project and which serves the sponsor's release date
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a GitHub issue list glowing beside a sponsor email with too many compliments

exampleSpecs.domain: community theatre casting committee after a donor's nephew auditions
exampleSpecs.audience: Isabel, a stage manager watching compliments change after the donor enters the lobby
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether reputation and local approval distort a casting choice the audience will notice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Isabel asks the committee to score the audition sheets before discussing the donor connection, keeping approval pressure from rewriting memory
exampleSpecs.firstImage: dust from the stage curtain hanging in a warm rehearsal room

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital nurse shift swap that looks generous but hides burnout risk
exampleSpecs.audience: Hadiya, a charge nurse asked to approve a fourth swap between the same two nurses
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether reciprocity pressure creates unsafe fatigue on a night shift
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hadiya maps the last four swaps on the staffing board and notices the favor debt is overriding rest rules
exampleSpecs.firstImage: colored magnets crowded around a night-shift staffing board

exampleSpecs.domain: real estate referral where a friend recommends an inspector
exampleSpecs.audience: Jack, a first-time buyer who trusts the friend but sees the referral fee disclosure
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether similarity and friendship make a conflicted recommendation feel safer than it is
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Jack places the disclosure form beside the inspection quote and calls two unaffiliated inspectors before accepting the friendly recommendation
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see the referral disclosure folded under a house key on the cafe table

exampleSpecs.domain: student engineering society choosing an award winner after one team helped everyone else
exampleSpecs.audience: Marta, a treasurer trying to separate gratitude from merit scoring
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether reciprocity turns a technical award into a thank-you note
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marta asks judges to predict their winner before seeing the peer-favor log, then compares how gratitude changes their rankings
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a peer-favor log with names highlighted in yellow

skillTargets: distinguish cynical motive-reading from incentive analysis
identify mixed motives in a scene
spot reciprocity and status pressure without assuming bad faith

tryThisNowSpec: Before one request or explanation today, write the stated reason, the material payoff, and the reputational payoff on three separate lines.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
